blocks.title: Observe
blocks.text: Clock speed counts clock cycles per second; one cycle is not always one complete instruction. Frequency alone cannot predict program performance.

blocks.title: Explain
blocks.text: Multiple CPU cores improve performance most for work divided into independently executable threads; a strictly sequential task may gain little.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Cache is small, fast storage close to CPU. A cache hit avoids some slower RAM accesses; cache size, locality and hit rate influence results.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the mechanism
blocks.text: 3 GHz offers 50% more cycles each second than2 GHz; this does not universally imply 50% faster program runtime. The comparison requires equal microarchitecture and workload assumptions.

questions.feedback: GHz — Billions of cycles per second.

blocks.title: Explain the mechanism
blocks.text: It may not be substantially faster from extra cores alone; only one thread is the bottleneck. Parallel benefits need tasks/threads that can run concurrently.
